subject: Tenant data flexibility: region-by-tenant storage and adjustable retention windows
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: SaaS Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>, legalops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-level retention + per-region placement questions (Acme pilot)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the notes and asked for two capabilities that are blockers for our pilot:

1) Tenant-scoped retention windows so we can set different TTLs per customer (some customers require 30 days, some 7 years).
2) The ability to pin a tenant's storage to a specific region (US east, EU, etc.) and ensure metadata and persisted embeddings remain in that region.

I've attached a short requirements matrix (acme_req_matrix.xlsx) with our baseline asks and compliance mappings. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant retention and regional residency today, and if not, what the engineering roadmap / expected delivery timeline looks like?

Our legal ops also wants to know whether deletion requests and retention policies are auditable (who initiated delete, when, and what records were removed).

We are targeting a pilot in Q3 and need to understand if there are gating platform changes or if we can proceed under a limited pilot with contractual guardrails.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with procurement and legal.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Integrations, Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_req_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12kb)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + per-region placement questions (Acme pilot)

Hi Jane — thanks for the matrix and the clear asks. Looping in Lauren and Karthik to give a read on product and engineering feasibility. Quick answers up front:

- Short answer: We do not currently expose per-tenant region pinning or arbitrary per-tenant TTLs in the hosted product as a self-serve toggle.
- We do have building blocks that help (tenant-scoped metadata, KV-backed object placement on dedicated/private deployments, and audit logging hooks).

Can the team please answer:
1) For an initial pilot, are ACME's customers willing to accept a hybrid approach where data for the pilot's tenants is placed in a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool in a US region (so residency is enforced by capacity placement) while we add a config layer for per-tenant TTL?
2) Legal is asking about the exact audit trails required (event-level vs. aggregated). Jane, can you paste a sample audit entry example from your compliance team?

I want to provide ACME a concise roadmap and a recommended plan (pilot + delivery milestones). Lauren / Karthik, can you propose a resource estimate and timeline we could share with the customer?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + per-region placement questions (Acme pilot)

Hi all — technical overview and proposed timeline from Product/Engineering: 

Summary of current state:
- Hosted: multi-tenant pools with best-effort regional affinity; no tenant-level storage pinning UI. TTLs are global per-model/config at present. Audit logs capture request-level events for hosted API keys but do not yet include a delete-event delta that enumerates removed token/embedding ids.
- Dedicated/Private: supports physical placement and can be deployed to a customer-specified region; more control over data locality and storage lifecycle is possible today via config and deployment choices.

Roadmap options (recommended path for ACME pilot):
Option A (fast pilot, minimal infra changes) — 6 weeks
- Create a dedicated US pool for the pilot tenants (Redwood Dedicated) to guarantee region of storage.
- Implement a tenant configuration flag (pilot-only) that maps a tenant to the dedicated pool.
- Surface a limited admin endpoint for per-tenant TTLs (30/90/365 days) backed by our existing deletion worker.
- Provide a scoped audit export: request-level logs + deletion events for pilot tenants.
Deliverable: pilot readiness in ~6 weeks with E2E verification and a scripted rollback.

Option B (full product feature) — 3 months
- Build first-class tenant-residency control in the control plane (UI + API) with region tags.
- Expand TTL config to arbitrary values per tenant and add background safe-delete with provenance records (who/when/object ids).
- Extend audit pipeline to include deletion deltas and retention policy versioning.
Deliverable: GA-grade feature for self-serve customers in ~3 months (requires more engineering + QA).

Engineering effort and risks:
- Option A: low-medium engineering cost, operational overhead for dedicated pilot pools.
- Option B: medium-high engineering cost, necessary for wider market but requires additional work on audit pipeline and compliance proofs (SOC-compliant exports).

Attachments: I attached a short proposal (redwood-proposal-tenant-options.pdf) with milestone dates and a rough SOW.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm Acme's appetite for the dedicated-pool pilot (Option A).
2) If yes, sign a short pilot addendum and select up to 5 tenants for piloting.
3) Product will schedule the 6-week pilot sprint and provide weekly status updates.

Happy to join a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow if you want to walk through trade-offs.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Management — Data Controls
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposal-tenant-options.pdf (PDF, 48kb)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com, legalops@acme-corp.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + per-region placement questions (Acme pilot)

Jane — thanks for the quick back-and-forth and for reviewing the proposal. Per Lauren's note, our recommended path to unblock your pilot quickly is Option A (dedicated US pool + pilot-only per-tenant TTLs).

Action items and owners:
- Acme: confirm willingness to proceed with dedicated-pool approach and share the list of up to 5 pilot tenant IDs (due EOD Tue). (Owner: Jane / Procurement)
- Redwood: provide pilot addendum (legal) and schedule the 6-week delivery sprint once addendum signed. (Owner: Marcus / Legal)
- Engineering: create the admin endpoint for per-tenant TTLs and enable audit export for pilot tenants. (Owner: Karthik / Product)

I'll have Legal draft the pilot addendum and send a DocuSign link this week. If procurement wants an explicit SLA or rollback guarantees we can include those in the addendum; otherwise we'll use standard pilot terms.

Jane — can you confirm by Tue whether procurement is comfortable with the dedicated-pool pilot? We'll also run a short technical readiness call (30 min) next week — I'll coordinate times.

Thanks everyone.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-pilot-addendum-draft.docx (referenced, not attached in thread)
